messages:
devon: starting kernel rollout 6.4.0 -> eu-central-1 p4 canary group now
infra-bot: rollout job #rk-342 started on 12 hosts (canary subset)
sara: seeing modprobe failures on canary-2 immediately after boot
sara: log: `modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/6.4.0-`
lia: dkms rebuild is failing on multiple nodes, symbols missing
lia: snippet: `ERROR: modpost: nvidia.ko: Unknown symbol in module`
raj: dmesg shows "nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol nvidia_pci_read" on canary-3
mike: paused the remainder of the rollout, cordoned the rest of eu-central-1 hosts
devon: copy of the dmesg and dkms output? need root cause quickly
sara: pasting quick logs below and uploading full tarball to gs://redwood-logs/kernel-rollback/1865432109.tar.gz
lia: also seeing `nvidia_drm: failed to register with DRM` and deferred probe messages
raj: NCCL jobs failing with handshake timeouts when scheduled on these nodes, cluster-level impact already visible
ops-oncall: opening incident, tagging SRE and infra leads
infra-bot: incident created INC-2026-7890: "kernel-6.4-driver-bind-failures-eu-central"
mike: immediate mitigation: rolling back canary hosts to kernel 5.15 snapshot and rebooting them into the previous image
sara: executing rollback now: `sudo apt-get install linux-image-5.15.0-104 && sudo update-grub && reboot`
devon: planner: 1) rollback canary hosts 2) hold rollout 3) run DKMS/kernel-abi job 4) vendor escalation for driver ABI change
lia: short-term workaround idea: boot with module blacklist for suspect nvidia modules and let jobs schedule elsewhere, but if modprobe missing, that won't help
raj: note: DKMS failure appears tied to kernel-headers path change in 6.4 and our bootstrap script assumes /usr/src/linux-headers-<ver>
lia: patch in infra-scripts repo that alters headers lookup landed in branch fix/kernel-headers-6x (PR: infra-scripts#234)
sara: will test the patched bootstrap on a spare host after rollback completes
mike: capacity note — provisioning extra on-demand p4s in us-west2 to drain training jobs will spike cost ~40% for the next 24h if we need to keep them up
ops-oncall: requesting approvals for temporary capacity from finance; tracking cost impact in the incident doc
devon: assign tasks: @sara - rollback + validate, @lia - DKMS bootstrap patch verification, @raj - NCCL job reschedule and logs aggregation, @mike - capacity and cloud requests
sara: rollback done on canary-2 and canary-3, they booted to 5.15 and drivers load fine again
lia: verified DKMS rebuild succeeds on 5.15, failing on 6.4 until our bootstrap fix is applied
raj: rescheduling affected training pods to healthy nodes; some checkpoints lost but most jobs resumed with restart policies
deploy-bot: deployment hold applied to kernel-rollout/rk-342
devon: next steps: merge DKMS/bootstrap fix, run a targeted canary with the patched bootstrap + vendor driver for 6.4 if available, add kernel-ABI gate to rollout pipeline
lia: also adding an automated preflight check to validate module build against kernel-headers on images before marking host healthy (CI job request created)
mike: will keep standby on-demand capacity for 24h and watch evictions/capacity pressure dashboards
ops-oncall: ETA for full recovery of affected jobs ~3 hours from now, keep incident open until all canaries validated or rollback complete
sara: thumbs up, logging postmortem notes in incident doc and will add exact commands used for rollback
devon: good catch all, nice triage. let's use this to tighten preflight and catch header/path changes earlier
sara: :thumbsup:
